Prefixing a function with @ turns its implicit arguments into explicit arguments.
However, in the output of the #check command, curly braces {} remain, which makes it look as though the arguments are still implicit.

/-- info: id.{u} {α : Sort u} (a : α) : α -/
#guard_msgs in
#check id

/-- info: @id : {α : Sort u_1} → α → α -/
#guard_msgs in
#check @id

Is this a bug, or is this behavior intentional?
prefixing with an @ does not turn the implicit arguments into explicit arguments, it disables the automatic insertion of implicit arguments
so when I write id 0, the α argument is inserted automatically, but if I write @id Nat, the α is not automatically inserted so Nat is used for α
@Aaron Liu Thank you. You saved me
